what: Reference frame invalidation (RFI) against the browser's WebCodecs decoders (spikes/s8-rfi): the S7 bench streamer on gpu-node (RTX 4090; test pattern at the bench page's size (about 1792×1008: the picture follows the page's element), 60 fps with 20 % noise, ~40 Mbit/s target) dumps each codec's first frames with CHA_DUMP_RFI=/tmp/rfi,120,3, as if frames 120-122 were lost: before encoding frame 123 it invalidates 120-122, so 123 is a recovery frame. The page, in the Claude desktop app's built-in browser (Chromium 152) on the M4 Pro, decodes each codec with all frames and without 120-122, with prefer-hardware and prefer-software, and compares the luma plane of frames 123-138.
notes: identical: every compared luma plane was bit-exact against the decode with all frames. worstPsnrDb: the lowest luma PSNR over the compared frames (null when identical).

Control: three frames nothing was invalidated for (116-118) are skipped and frame 119 is compared. controlPsnrDb: its luma PSNR against the full decode. controlError: the decoder raised an error instead.
HEVC software decode is not offered by Chromium (VideoDecoder.isConfigSupported is false for prefer-software), so identical is null there.
First run, with a 5-frame DPB (cha-nvenc's DPB_FRAMES is now 8); the three lost frames fit in either.
NVENC (driver 595.71.05) reports NV_ENC_CAPS_SUPPORT_REF_PIC_INVALIDATION for H.264, HEVC and AV1 and produced a P-frame for 123 in each.

frameBytes: encoded sizes in bytes. key: the first (key) frame; p119: the P-frame before the loss; recovery123: the recovery frame; p124: the P-frame after it. A recovery frame costs what a P-frame does; a keyframe costs 2.4-3.3 times as much (here with a one-frame VBV).

H.264 and AV1 decoders raise no error on a missing reference and show a different picture instead (the control's 17.9 and 14.5 dB), so the page must never feed a frame past a loss except a keyframe or a recovery frame.

laterRuns.result: identical on every decoder (H.264 and AV1 hardware and software, HEVC hardware)
identical on every decoder; the live page played 4K at 59-60 fps with nothing lost
